title: Where work waits: a bottleneck, and what a change does to it
audience: Operations, service and shared-services teams explaining why work backs up and what a capacity change does
inputs: Arrivals per period and each stage's capacity per period (stated assumptions), and the change to show

beats.vo: Ten requests arrive each day. Review finishes eight, so two more wait every day. After a second reviewer joins, the queue drains two a day; it does not vanish.

sources.claim: Arrival and capacity rates are illustrative assumptions for a model, not measurements.

note: The model is serial and deterministic: the numbers on screen are computed from the rates you state, period by period, and a change carries the queue it inherits. Say in the narration that it is an illustration of the stated rates. Every figure and rule here is an illustrative sample: replace it with your source's before publishing.
